subject: Next steps: retention & deletion SLAs (logs/backup)
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Long <timothy.long@clearhealth.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + retention / deletion notes

Tim — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we covered:
- ClearHealth needs clarity on log retention, backup retention, and guaranteed deletion (esp. deletion from backups).
- Questions about SOC 2 status and supporting artifacts, encryption and KMS controls for backups, and scope for HIPAA/GDPR regulated workloads.

Immediate clarifications (from Redwood):
- SOC 2: Redwood is in the final stages of a Type II assessment; we expect a completed report Q1 2027. We can provide a readiness summary and control mapping now (attached upon request).
- Encryption: All customer data in transit is TLS; at rest we use AES-256. For Redwood Private customers we offer customer-managed KMS/HSM integration.
- Default retention (hosted API): request logs and runtime traces retained 90 days; conversational payloads (customer data) 30 days by default. Backup snapshots are retained 180 days in our standard offering, with configurable shorter or longer windows for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Deletion SLA: deletion requests remove live data within 24 hours and we guarantee removal from recoverable backups within 30–90 days depending on archival class; we can discuss a contractual 30-day deletion SLA for enterprise customers with dedicated retention policies.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send our retention SLA excerpt and a one-page SOC 2 readiness summary (we can redline SLA if needed).
2) Laura (cc) will initiate the vendor security questionnaire/doc and an NDA if required.
3) Marcus (cc) can join a technical deep-dive to go over encryption, backups, and deletion mechanics — propose Wed 10/12 or Thu 10/13.

Please confirm which artifacts you want first (SLA excerpt, SOC2 readiness summary, or full questionnaire) and whether you prefer us to use the DocuSign NDA link or your procurement template.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
David Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
+david.kim@redwood.com
From: Timothy Long <timothy.long@clearhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + retention / deletion notes

David — appreciate the summary. A few follow-ups from our security team before we lock next steps:

1) Backups: are your backups encrypted with customer keys or Redwood-managed keys by default? For ClearHealth we need to know if we can require CMK (customer-managed keys) for hosted production data. Also: are backups replicated across regions or single region by default?
2) Deletion: when you say removal from recoverable backups within 30–90 days, does that include deep-archive copies (cold storage)? Our legal team expects a written guarantee that data is not recoverable after the stated SLA.
3) SOC 2 artifacts: we need the current control mapping and any evidence you can share now (readiness docs, policy excerpts). A completed Type II report would be ideal but we understand timing.
4) HIPAA/GDPR: do you provide a BAA and data processing addendum? If so, can you share a template or point to where we can review it?

Marcus from our side will coordinate the technical answers — looping him in. We'll want Marcus (security) and our procurement lead on the follow-up call. 

If you can send the SLA excerpt and the vendor questionnaire form, we'll circulate internally and propose times for the deep-dive.

Best,
Timothy
Head of Platform Security
ClearHealth
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Vendor security questionnaire + NDA (initial)

Tim — Laura from Legal here. Following David's note, I'm attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire (document attached as a working copy). If ClearHealth prefers to push your questionnaire instead, we can start with that.

Quick items from Legal: 
- We'll provide a redlineable BAA/DPA template for HIPAA/GDPR once we confirm the commercial terms.
- For SOC 2: we can provide a control mapping and interim evidence (policy documents, architecture diagrams). Full Type II report will be shared when available.
- Please confirm whether you require a mutual NDA prior to exchanging internal artifacts; we can send a DocuSign link if helpful.

Action: I'll kick off the questionnaire and would appreciate your security team's preliminary answers in the next 5 business days so Marcus (Redwood infra) can follow up on technical items.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Long <timothy.long@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + retention / deletion notes

Tim — attaching the two artifacts we discussed:
- redwood-sla-retention-2026.pdf (excerpt with deletion SLA options and backup retention classes)
- redwood-soc2-readiness-summary.pdf (control mapping and high-level schedule)

Quick answers inline to your questions:
- Keys: hosted-managed backups use Redwood-managed KMS by default (AWS KMS with strict access controls). For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed KMS. We can add a contractual requirement for CMK in the hosted plan for enterprise customers if ClearHealth requires it.
- Replication: standard hosted configuration stores backup snapshots in the primary region; cross-region replication is available as an opt-in feature for DR and immutability requirements.
- Deep-archive: deep-archive (cold) classes are not part of the default 30-day deletion SLA; if ClearHealth wants a 30-day guaranteed removal including deep-archive we will need to include an archival purge clause in the contract. Typical timelines: live data purge <24 hours; recoverable backups purge target 30 days; archival purge up to 90 days unless contracted otherwise.
- BAA/DPA: we have a BAA template and DPA we can share — Laura will lead that.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CLH-2026-042
- Proposed NDA: https://docusign.com/example/CLH-NDA-2026

Next step: please confirm whether you want us to commit to 30 days across all storage classes (live + backups + archive) or whether a split SLA (30 days live + 90 days archive) is acceptable as baseline. We can prepare a contractual redline once you confirm.

—
David Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-sla-retention-2026.pdf, redwood-soc2-readiness-summary.pdf

Thanks — the artifacts look good as a starting point. We will: 
- Circulate the vendor questionnaire and the SLA excerpt to our security and legal teams today.
- Marcus (security) will coordinate a technical deep-dive; tentative call on Mon 10/12 at 11:00 PT (we'll confirm).
- Regarding deletion SLA: our procurement prefers a 30-day full purge (live + backups + archives). If Redwood requires an archival carve-out, please include the proposed archival purge timeline in the contract redline.

We'll also need the BAA template before the deep-dive so our legal team can review. If you can send the DocuSign NDA, we'll execute that and return the questionnaire answers within 3-5 business days.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll be in touch.

Best,
Timothy Long
Head of Platform Security
ClearHealth
